title: The symmetric algebra of a quotient module is the quotient of the symmetric algebra by the ideal generated by the kernel
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $p:N\to M$ a surjective homomorphism of $R$-modules with kernel $K=\ker p$. Let $\operatorname{Sym}_R(N),\iota_N$ and $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M),\iota_M$ be the symmetric algebras and their canonical $R$-linear maps [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property], and $\operatorname{Sym}(p):\operatorname{Sym}_R(N)\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ the unique $R$-algebra homomorphism with $\operatorname{Sym}(p)(\iota_N(x))=\iota_M(p(x))$ for $x\in N$. Then $\operatorname{Sym}(p)$ is surjective and its kernel is the ideal of $\operatorname{Sym}_R(N)$ generated by $\iota_N(K)$; so $\operatorname{Sym}(p)$ induces an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\operatorname{Sym}_R(N)/(\iota_N(K))\cong\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DO (lemma-presentation-sym-exterior, line 2241; proof omitted in the source): for an exact sequence M_2 -> M_1 -> M -> 0 the sequences M_2 (x) Sym^{n-1}(M_1) -> Sym^n(M_1) -> Sym^n(M) -> 0 are exact. With M_1 = N, M_2 = K, the image of K (x) Sym^{n-1}(N) in Sym^n(N) is iota_N(K) * Sym^{n-1}(N), and the sum over n >= 1 of these is the ideal generated by iota_N(K); so the statement is 00DO summed over all degrees n (degree 0: Sym^0 = R on both sides)

proof.text: The universal property of the symmetric algebra applied to the R-linear map iota_M composed with p gives a unique R-algebra homomorphism Sym(p): Sym_R(N) -> Sym_R(M) satisfying Sym(p)(iota_N(x)) = iota_M(p(x)).

source.place: Algebra, Section 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), universal property of the symmetric algebra

proof.text: Apply the degreewise exactness of Lemma 00DO to the exact sequence K -> N -> M -> 0, where K = ker(p) and the first map is the inclusion. For every n >= 1, the degree-n component of Sym(p) is surjective and its kernel is the image of K tensor Sym^{n-1}(N) under multiplication by iota_N(K).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DO (lemma-presentation-sym-exterior, line 2241), summed over the graded pieces

proof.text: The symmetric algebra is the direct sum of its homogeneous pieces. Therefore the preceding degreewise surjectivity makes Sym(p) surjective, and its kernel is the direct sum of the degree-n images of K tensor Sym^{n-1}(N), together with the zero degree component. The latter is zero because Sym(p) is the identity on R. The positive-degree sum is exactly the ideal generated by iota_N(K): multiplying a generator iota_N(k) by a homogeneous element of degree n-1 gives the indicated image, and every element of the generated ideal is a finite sum of such products.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DO (lemma-presentation-sym-exterior, line 2241), identification of the summed images with the ideal generated by iota_N(K)

proof.text: The first isomorphism theorem for commutative R-algebras identifies Sym_R(N) modulo this kernel ideal with Sym_R(M), yielding Sym_R(N)/(iota_N(K)) ≅ Sym_R(M).
